amanda: quick follow-up to the streaming retries doc — we need a concrete approach for handling transient client disconnects vs. real upstream failures. My proposal: keep short-lived in-flight buffers at edge, allow resume-window of 5s, and only trigger a backend retry after idempotency token check fails. sketch: 1) accept stream, 2) assign stream_id + resume_nonce, 3) local buffer up to 32KB, 4) if client reconnects within window -> resume, else forward abort to backend and maybe retry.

raj: +1 on resume windows, but how do we guarantee ordering with hedging? if we hedge to a fallback, resumed client might get duplicate tokens.

sylvia: we should tie hedging to seq numbers in the resume_nonce. if hedged path produces tokens with seq > resume_point then we can fast-forward; otherwise we need dedupe at application layer. also memory pressure: local buffers need LRU/eviction; maybe use per-tenant soft cap.

tom: question: what about long polls / polling clients that send very small chunks? keeping buffers for them is costly. Could we switch them to non-resumable short-path with explicit 409 if client asks to resume beyond window?

amanda: that's reasonable. new mental model: traffic pattern -> small-chunk clients default to non-resumable, large streaming sessions get resume enabled via header `x-rwd-resume: true` and an expected-chunk-frequency hint.

raj: operations: how do we account for cost? buffers + resume metadata across millions of connections could be huge. suggest: per-gw shard limit and evict oldest per-customer. add metrics: resume_hit/miss, evicted_sessions.

sylvia: implementation detail: reuse existing session store rather than adding a new one. we can piggyback on connection metadata we already store for session affinity; just extend with resume_nonce and a small circular buffer pointer.

amanda: edge case: what if backend accepts then stalls (writes some tokens, blocks), client reconnects and sees partial output? need to ensure idempotency on the backend or be able to fetch KV cache state. proposal: store last-applied-kv-version with resume_nonce. backend must expose a lightweight "resume-check" API that returns whether a resume is safe.

tom: can we avoid backend changes? maybe by forcing a fallback to re-run from the last full checkpoint when resume-check isn't available. expensive but safer.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: edge-resume-window feature flag rollout starting 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. :rocket:

raj: notes for RFC follow-up: document invariants: ordering, at-most-once vs at-least-once semantics, memory bounds, metrics. Will draft a small state diagram.

amanda: thanks. action items: raj to draft invariants + metrics; sylvia + tom to prototype buffer LRU; i'll write the external API spec for `resume-check` and the header-based enable. Let's sync Fri 9am PT. :calendar:

sylvia: ping — I'll add some pseudo-API later: 
```
POST /edge/resume-check
{ \"stream_id\": \"s_123\", \"resume_nonce\": \"n_456\", \"last_seq\": 42 }
=> { \"resume_ok\": true, \"backend_kv_version\": \"kv_789\" }
```

tom: if resume_ok false -> respond 409 with `resume_window_expired` and optional `checkpoint_id`.

amanda: perfect. keeping this thread for notes — please add short single-line comments rather than long threads. :pray:
